about.title: West Hollywood Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision reshapes everything, and West Hollywood families are often left sorting through grief while facing unanswered questions about how the crash happened. Los Angeles County records show traffic deaths occur here even amid a much larger volume of injury collisions, and corridors such as Sunset Boulevard, Santa Monica Boulevard, Fountain Avenue, and La Cienega Boulevard see regular reported activity, including a noted rise in crashes on Sunday nights between midnight and 2 a.m. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a wrongful death claim to recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and can help your family reach an independent attorney who handles these matters on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An independent attorney can help clarify where your family fits.

items.title: Awareness of the Filing Deadline
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity require faster action. Missing this window can end a family's ability to recover.

items.title: Recovering What the Law Allows
items.desc: Beyond funeral and burial costs, California law recognizes lost financial support and the loss of a loved one's companionship and guidance as recoverable losses. An attorney can help document these losses accurately.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have first priority to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm eligibility.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in West Hollywood?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim. If a government entity, such as the City of West Hollywood or Los Angeles County, may be involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires prompt action. Because timing matters, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as possible.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal charges that may be filed against a driver. Even if criminal proceedings are ongoing or resolved differently than a family hoped, the civil claim proceeds on its own track. This distinction can matter for families navigating both processes at once.
